key_insight: AI-related clinical trials have risen sharply over time, with newer terms like chatbots, GPTs, and large language models appearing more often.
clinical_relevance: Better tracking of AI terminology and human-AI interaction in trial registries can improve trial discovery, reporting, and oversight.
method: Analyzed ClinicalTrials.gov records to map temporal and geographic trends in AI-related trials.
Used a hybrid workflow combining a frontier generative AI model (GPT-5.5) with human review to screen and categorize records.
Compared human and AI classifications in a random sample of 100 records.
evidence_signal: The sample evaluation found good human-AI agreement for identifying studies not truly using AI, but weaker agreement for classifying human-AI interaction, especially when reporting was unclear.
watch_item: Ambiguous or underreported trial descriptions can make human-AI interaction categories hard to classify reliably.
paper_title: Trends in AI and Human-AI Interaction in Clinical Trials -- A Hybrid Human-AI Exploration
